title: Head-to-head: same 'build a working Excel in Next.js + shadcn' prompt; Claude Code's version doubled typed letters and got SUM wrong, Cursor (Opus 4.6 agent) got formulas working

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: run via terminal, output had input-doubling and wrong SUM

tools.name: Cursor
tools.detail: Agent mode, model 'Opus 4.6' per the on-screen chat, Local, 'Try Plan Mode'

claims: Claude Code's Excel clone looked good but doubled every typed letter and computed =SUM(B2:B4) incorrectly
Cursor's build with the identical prompt rendered the same UI and =SUM(B2:B4) worked
Creator scores the round to Cursor and asks why people moved from Cursor to Claude Code
how_to_steps: Paste the prompt into Claude Code, run npm run dev, test typing and a SUM formula
Paste the exact same prompt into Cursor Agent, let it run the app, repeat the tests
on_screen_only: Title card 'Claude Code vs Cursor Building Excel' with checkbox scoreboard; Claude Code gets a red X by the end
Claude Code welcome screen: 'Make a CLAUDE.md file for instructions. Claude will read it every single time.'; terminal 'cd ... && npm run dev'

Cursor chat prompt: 'Build a working version of Excel with next.js and shadcn. I want basic formulas working. Don't worry about authentication and backend, do everything on the front-end.' with 'Agent', 'Opus 4.6', 'Local', 'Try Plan Mode'
Both spreadsheets: columns Month/Revenue, rows Jan 1000, Feb 3000, Mar 4000; formula bar '=SUM(B2:B4)'; Cursor result shows '8,000'
cta: comment why you moved from Cursor to Claude Code

relevance.why: A single-run anecdote; the Claude Code bug is the kind of thing one follow-up prompt fixes. Not a basis for tool choice

implement_score.why: Nothing to adopt; at most a reminder to test a generated UI before judging it

verify: Which model/version Claude Code used (not shown) versus Cursor's Opus 4.6
Whether the Claude Code run was given a second turn to fix the bug (n=1 comparison)

gap.what: Anecdotal one-shot comparison with no technique, tool or correction worth keeping
